articles.title: In 2014, a Palm Beach couple paid $9 million for a dated 1955 waterfront house, rebuilt it through an extensive renovation, then sold the Everglades Island estate 11 years later for $25.4 million
articles.summary: Cornelia ‘Cornie’ Thornburgh and her husband, Richard, have sold their renovated lakefront mansion and guest house on Everglades Island in the
articles.body: Cornelia ‘Cornie’ Thornburgh and her husband, Richard, have sold their renovated lakefront mansion and guest house on Everglades Island in the Intracoastal Waterway, the Palm Beach Post reported.The house at 550 Island Drive was listed at $24.9 million, according to the multiple listing service. The deed, recorded on Jan. 10, 2025, shows a price of $25.4 million. The buyer is 260N Property Limited Partnership, which is registered in Manitoba and uses a mailing address at an office building in Toronto.Buyer already has land across townThe buyer is not new to Palm Beach. It owns a four-bedroom house at 260 N. Woods Road in the North End. It paid about $6.28 million for the 1977 house in September 2020. In March 2022, it added the empty lot next door at 254 N. Woods Road for $9.25 million. That lot is about a third of an acre.The house and lot are now on the market together for $22.9 million, the listing service shows. Agent Jim McCann of Premier Estate Properties holds that listing. He also represented the buyer in the Island Drive deal.The Island Drive estate did not sell quickly. The agents, Liza Pulitzer and Whitney McGurk of Brown Harris Stevens, first listed it in April 2023 at $39 million. After several price cuts, its final price landed about $13.6 million below that first asking price.The Thornburghs bought for $9 millionBuilt in 1955, the mansion sits on about half an acre, with 150 feet of frontage on the canal that separates the island from the Everglades Golf Course. The Thornburghs bought the property in 2014 for $9 million. They felt the mansion needed a gut renovation. “This house was dated and a bit of a wreck. We saw that it was a project, but we also knew it was a special place,” Cornie Thornburgh told the Palm Beach Daily News in 2023.The couple hired architect Jacqueline Albarran of SKA Architect+Planners. Contractor Tim Givens of Tim Givens Building & Remodeling Inc. ran the work. The team changed the layout of the main house a great deal but kept the focus on the water views and the thick mangroves along the golf course. “Not one thing went untouched,” Thornburgh said in the same interview.Inside the renovated mansionThe Thornburghs went for a massive renovation. The main house now has five bedrooms, four of them on the ground floor, along with a den and access to a two-car garage. The living and dining rooms open to a poolside lanai. The main suite is upstairs and has a balcony facing the gorgeous water.Wide-plank hardwood floors run through the rooms. The vaulted ceilings in limed wood are another highlight. The mansion also has gas fireplaces in the living room and lanai, setting the tone. The kitchen has custom cabinets and high-end appliances. A two-bedroom guest house and cabana building also sit nearby. After the renovations, the couple named the property Pelican Strait. The Palm Beach couple were keen on hosting parties, and their entertaining space can host about 100 people. “We have had parties here for 100 people, and now the house flows well. In so many big houses, you ramble around, but this house is cosy and comfortable when there’s no kids around and it’s just the two of us,” the couple said.The Thornburghs had to downsize, so they moved to a 1920s bungalow at 159 Australian Ave., just east of the police headquarters near Town Hall. They bought the historic home in 2023 from Amy Tarrant for $8.12 million. The 4,436-square-foot home has five bedrooms. The town gave it landmark protection in 2013, and earlier owners won an award from the Preservation Foundation of Palm Beach for restoring it. Elizabeth Woody of Compass Florida represented both sides of that sale.Prior to owning the mansion on Island Drive, the couple owned another landmarked house, a 1923 villa on Golfview Road. Richard Thornburgh, a senior adviser at private-equity firm Corsair Capital LLC, also has ties to New York, but the latest tax rolls list the Island Drive house as their main home.The estate is the seventh house north of the short bridge that links Everglades Island to the rest of town through Island Road. articles.title: Colorado police sergeant reveals how human traffickers target vulnerable children: ‘Happening in our backyard’
articles.summary: The Aurora Police Department Human Trafficking Unit recovered 29 survivors, including 15 minors, in its first year by targeting exploitation of vulnerable youth.
articles.body: Human traffickers are turning children’s hunger, desperation and need for affection into tools of exploitation, a Colorado city police sergeant warned after his dedicated unit’s first year brought dozens of survivors to safety. The Aurora Police Department (APD) Human Trafficking Unit opened 53 investigations, arrested 28 suspects and recovered 29 survivors, including 15 minors, in its first year. APD Sgt. Joseph Sullivan told Fox News Digital the work is exposing abuse that residents may never suspect is happening around them. According to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), "human trafficking involves the use of force, fraud, or coercion to obtain some type of labor or commercial sex act." MIKE WALTZ, TIM TEBOW LAUNCH EFFORT TO COMBAT ONLINE CHILD EXPLOITATION: 'IT'S HAPPENING IN THEIR BACKYARD' "It is happening in our backyard, not just in those other places," Sullivan said. For Sullivan, one teenage girl’s plea captures both the urgency of that mission and the difficult road survivors face after investigators reach them. The 16-year-old had been brought to Aurora — a city of just over 400,000 people outside Denver — from another town by her boyfriend, who then left her there, Sullivan said. Trying to survive, she was sexually exploited by people around an apartment complex in exchange for somewhere to stay, drugs or food. SIX UNDERAGE GIRLS RECOVERED IN SWEEPING OPERATION TARGETING NOTORIOUS TRAFFICKING CORRIDOR During an interview, she asked a detective to find those responsible. "'I really hope that you can find the people that are doing this, because it really hurts what I’m having to do just to survive,'" Sullivan recalled her saying. The girl died of an overdose a few months later, he said. Her words stayed with him. "It really is satisfying being able to contact these survivors and then identify who’s exploiting them and holding them accountable," Sullivan said. FLORIDA-LED OPERATION RESCUES 163 CHILDREN AROUND GLOBE IN HISTORIC STATE SWEEP, HUNTS SUSPECTED PREDATORS But reaching someone does not guarantee an immediate or lasting escape. Survivors may need repeated contact, resources and offers of help before they can find a way out, he said. That is part of why having dedicated detectives matters. Created in September 2025, the trafficking unit has three detectives and a supervising sergeant. Sullivan said its focus is sex trafficking involving people 21 and younger, allowing the small team to concentrate its efforts. The investigations demand time to gather evidence, build cases and help victims feel comfortable enough to testify. "Having a dedicated unit helps lower their overall caseload and allows them to apply the time and effort that these cases deserve," Sullivan said. DOJ SAYS 11 MIGRANTS INDICTED IN MULTI-STATE SEX TRAFFICKING, DRUG, FIREARMS CASE APD Investigations Bureau Cmdr. Marc Paolino said the unit was built to put survivors at the center of investigations while targeting those exploiting them. "The work they’ve done has made our community safer and sent a clear message that the Aurora Police Department will aggressively pursue anyone who exploits others for this type of heinous, criminal activity," Paolino said in a department release. Among those arrested is Marshae Wheelock, 24, of Aurora, whom police linked to multiple cases allegedly involving the exploitation of children over several years. "Marshae Wheelock represents the type of offender the Human Trafficking Unit was created to investigate; someone who repeatedly preys on vulnerable children," APD Deputy Chief Mark Hildebrand said in the release. TRUMP SIGNS HAWLEY MEASURE ADDING 200 CHILD EXPLOITATION INVESTIGATORS IN LARGEST CRACKDOWN EFFORT YET The department also detailed a February undercover operation in which investigators recovered a 16-year-old girl and later identified three suspects accused of sexually exploiting her for financial gain. Sullivan cautioned that trafficking often looks very different from the abductions portrayed in movies. Someone does not have to be snatched off the street by another person to exploit their vulnerability. "There is some kind of need that a trafficker identifies to exploit, and that’s how they get in," Sullivan said. That need could be housing, food, money or affection. Filling it through legitimate support is a central part of helping survivors, he said. The APD works with human services officials, nonprofit organizations and victim advocates. Sullivan pointed to a local group, From Silence to Saved, which helps victims from the beginning of an investigation through court proceedings and afterward. MORE THAN 300 ARRESTED IN SPRAWLING CALIFORNIA CRACKDOWN ON CHILD EXPLOITATION CRIMES He also credited support from police leadership and organizations that provide tools to help detectives identify victims online. Sullivan oversees Aurora’s Internet Crimes Against Children team, as well as its trafficking detectives. The teams investigate distinct crimes, including sextortion, but their work can overlap. The department said the trafficking unit draws on local, state and federal partnerships, and investigative resources through the Colorado Cyber Guardian Task Force. The threats also cross geographic and economic boundaries. Asked whether Tren de Aragua (TdA) had been involved in the trafficking his team investigated, Sullivan said his unit had not encountered that connection. His broader point was that exploitation can affect people across backgrounds. Sullivan described another high school student who came from a wealthier background but became vulnerable after her mother suffered a disabling medical crisis and her father was absent. The girl became addicted to drugs and was exploited by someone else, he said. FBI AND TEXAS AUTHORITIES ARREST 276 SUSPECTED CHILD PREDATORS, RESCUE 89 CHILDREN IN SWEEPING OPERATION "There really is no boundary on where we see victims," Sullivan said. Investigators regularly work with other agencies, including when victims travel between states. "This is a problem in every community around the country, whether it’s a big city or small," he added. For parents, Sullivan’s advice begins with staying involved and asking questions about what their children are doing online. Warning signs can include unexplained cash, new clothes or paid-for manicures, as well as disappearing for a weekend and returning with things they did not have before. He encouraged families to use educational resources from the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children. Some investigations remain stalled while detectives await additional information, Sullivan said. Survivors may not be ready to come forward or may not recognize themselves as victims, making it harder to advance a case. As the unit enters its second year, its priorities remain identifying victims and building cases against those exploiting them. Public tips can help detectives reach people sooner, he said. "We don’t turn away any kind of tips," Sullivan said. He also urged people experiencing exploitation to seek support even if they are not ready to participate in a criminal investigation. Advocacy organizations can help without involving police, he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For the detectives, the mission continues beyond an arrest: working with partners to meet the needs traffickers used to gain control in the first place. "Using a group of people to help identify those needs and provide those needs is kind of the goal and the key to us being successful," Sullivan said.

articles.title: Govt caps trade margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs at 30% of MRP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The government on Thursday decided to cap trade margins at 30% of the maximum retail price (MRP) for all non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The government on Thursday decided to cap trade margins at 30% of the maximum retail price (MRP) for all non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, according to official sources cited by ANI.The decision will cover branded and generic medicines, as well as domestic and imported drugs, including patented and non-patented medicines. The government said the move is aimed at addressing excessive trade mark-ups and improving the affordability of life-saving cancer medicines while ensuring their continued availability.According to the official sources, the measure could result in up to 70% reduction in the MRP of the affected medicines and is expected to generate estimated annual savings of around Rs 2,500 crore for patients.Under the decision, the trade margin on all non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines will be capped at 30% of their MRP. The measure covers a wide range of medicines, irrespective of whether they are branded or generic, manufactured domestically or imported, or patented or non-patented.The government said the intervention is intended to tackle excessive mark-ups in the distribution and sale of cancer medicines and reduce the financial burden on patients.The move is also expected to lower out-of-pocket expenditure for cancer patients, according to official sources cited by ANI.The government has projected that the intervention could bring down the MRP of affected medicines by up to 70%.According to official estimates, the trade-margin cap is expected to result in annual savings of approximately Rs 2,500 crore.The savings are expected to accrue to patients through lower prices for the affected anti-cancer medicines.The government has also framed the measure as part of its broader effort to improve access to affordable medicines while maintaining the availability of essential treatments.The latest decision builds on a similar government intervention introduced in 2019.According to official sources cited by ANI, the 2019 measure resulted in reported annual savings of Rs 984 crore across 526 brands.The government said the latest intervention reinforces its focus on affordable and accessible healthcare, particularly for patients requiring expensive cancer treatment.The latest cap extends the approach to all non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs and covers medicines across different categories, including branded, generic, domestic, imported, patented and non-patented products.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Anne Carson: 'Bold and inventive' Canadian poet wins Nobel Prize in Literature
articles.summary: Carson, 76, is celebrated for works that often cross boundaries between poetry, fiction and scholarship.
articles.body:
Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson has been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Literature.

Carson, 76, is celebrated for works that often cross the boundaries between poetry, fiction and scholarship.

The Nobel Prize committee said they had selected her "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature".

The Nobel Prize is awarded for a lifetime's body of work and is regarded as the most prestigious award in global literature, with the winner receiving 12 million Swedish kronor (£900,000, $1.2m).

In 2019, her performance piece Norma Jeane Baker of Troy drew a line between famous beauties from different historical periouds - Helen of Troy and Marilyn Monroe.

In 2021, she released The Trojan Women: A Comic, a graphic retelling of Euripides' ancient story; and her translation of Elektra by Sophocles was staged starring Brie Larson in London last year.

Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, said she had broken the news to Carson on the phone shortly before the public announcement.

"She had time to tell me was that she is, for the moment, in Iceland, where she is listening to the wind," Carlberg, said.

"She was taken by surprise but very happy. I could hear that in her voice."

Born in Toronto in 1950, Carson lives in Michigan and has also held Icelandic citizenship since 2022.

Anders Olsson, chairman of the Swedish Academy's Nobel committee for Literature, praised the way Carson has "broken away from lyrical poetry bound to the narrative self and inspired new forms of contemporary literature".

"This method of writing leads to playful and ironic works that move not only between classical and modern poetry but also between different genres and artforms," he said.

Carson's notable works include The Glass Essay, Autobiography of Red: A Novel in Verse, Nox, Float and The Beauty of the Husband: A Fictional Essay in 29 Tangos.

She has been a professor of classics for more than 30 years and her writing is often inspired by Greek literature.

Her translations have often given a contemporary twist to ancient works.

"Her collaborations with visual artists and choreographers and with opera and theatre directors demonstrate the freedom with which she relates to literary expectations and rule systems," Olsson said.

"It is this that lies behind the outstanding importance her work since the 1990s has had for the international art and literature scene."

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian author Anne Carson, the Swedish Academy announced on Thursday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian author Anne Carson, the Swedish Academy announced on Thursday.2025: László KrasznahorkaiHungarian novelist and screenwriter László Krasznahorkai won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature for what the Swedish Academy described as his "compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art".Krasznahorkai, born in 1954 in Gyula, Hungary, is known for novels marked by long, winding sentences, bleak landscapes, absurdity and a persistent sense of impending catastrophe. His work often places individuals in societies marked by collapse, disorder and uncertainty.His international breakthrough came with his 1985 novel Satantango, a work that follows the inhabitants of a failing collective farm and explores manipulation, despair and the search for meaning. The book was later adapted into a celebrated seven-hour film by Hungarian director Béla Tarr.Another major work, The Melancholy of Resistance, published in 1989, centres on a travelling circus and a mysterious whale whose arrival throws a small Hungarian town into chaos. The novel explores social breakdown and the fragility of order.Krasznahorkai's work has also included War & War, Seiobo There Below and Baron Wenckheim's Homecoming. His writing has been translated into numerous languages and has earned him a reputation as one of the most distinctive contemporary European novelists.The Swedish Academy's citation focused not simply on the darkness in his writing but on the role of art within that darkness. His Nobel recognition therefore placed the idea of literature surviving and resisting chaos at the centre of the award.2024: Han KangA year earlier, the Nobel Prize in Literature went to South Korean writer Han Kang, making her the first South Korean recipient of the literature prize.The Swedish Academy honoured her "for her intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life".Born in Gwangju in 1970, Han Kang moved with her family to Seoul when she was nine. She began her literary career with poetry in 1993 before making her prose debut in 1995.Her international breakthrough came with The Vegetarian, originally published in South Korea in 2007 and later translated into English. The novel tells the story of Yeong-hye, a woman who abruptly decides to stop eating meat. What begins as a seemingly personal decision develops into a confrontation with family, social expectations, violence and control.The English translation of The Vegetarian, by Deborah Smith, won the International Booker Prize in 2016, helping introduce Han Kang's work to a much wider international readership.Han Kang's writing frequently explores the relationship between physical and psychological suffering. Her novels also return to questions of memory, violence, grief and the ways individuals carry the trauma of historical events.Her 2014 novel Human Acts deals with the 1980 Gwangju massacre, an event of particular personal significance because Han Kang was born in the city. The novel gives voice to victims of the military crackdown and examines the physical and emotional consequences of political violence.Another major work, The White Book, is built around grief and the death of an infant sister. Her later novel We Do Not Part explores the lingering trauma of the Jeju massacres of the late 1940s.The Swedish Academy said Han Kang's work confronts historical trauma and "exposes the fragility of human life", while also pointing to her distinctive understanding of the relationship between the body and the soul, and between the living and the dead.2023: Jon FosseBefore Han Kang, the 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature went to Norwegian author Jon Fosse, recognised "for his innovative plays and prose which give voice to the unsayable".Born in Haugesund, Norway, in 1959, Fosse has written across several forms, including novels, plays, poetry, essays, children's books and translations. Much of his work is written in Nynorsk, one of Norway's two official written forms of the Norwegian language.Fosse is particularly known as a playwright, with his work performed widely across Europe and beyond. His writing is often spare and repetitive, with pauses, silences and seemingly ordinary conversations used to explore loneliness, anxiety, death, relationships and spirituality.His debut novel, Raudt, svart, was published in 1983. His international breakthrough as a dramatist came with Someone Is Going to Come, first published in 1996 and later staged internationally.The Swedish Academy described Fosse's writing as giving expression to experiences that are difficult to put into words. His work often strips away conventional dramatic action and instead focuses on repetition, silence and the inner lives of his characters.Fosse's recognition also brought attention to a literary tradition rooted in Norway's Nynorsk language while using modernist techniques. The Nobel Committee noted that he combines strong local and linguistic roots with influences from modernist writers including Samuel Beckett and Thomas Bernhard.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Actor Sumeet Raghavan has called out tourists for littering in Himachal Pradesh after finding garbage scattered along the trail leading to the popular
articles.body: Actor Sumeet Raghavan has called out tourists for littering in Himachal Pradesh after finding garbage scattered along the trail leading to the popular Tattapani hot springs. During his visit, Raghavan and a few others collected some of the waste they found on the way and showed it in a video shared on Instagram. Raghavan said he was visiting Tattapani with a group associated with the Indus Paragliding School. The group included people from different professions, including Raghavan, who introduced himself as an actor, and Dushyant, an architect. As they made their way towards the hot springs, the group began collecting the garbage lying along the route. In the video, Raghavan showed the bag they had filled with the waste and pointed out that there was still much more litter scattered around them.“Hello guys, we have come to Himachal Pradesh to see Tata Pani Hot Springs. We are associated with a school called Indus Paragliding School. There are people from different professions here. I am an actor. Here is Dushyant. He is an architect. And many more people are coming from behind,” Raghavan said in the video. He then showed the garbage the group had picked up. “Now our bag is full, but there is so much garbage here,” he said.“It is such a beautiful place”Raghavan described the sight as shameful and questioned why visitors leave waste behind in a place known for its natural surroundings. “It is a very shameful thing that we are destroying such a good place. And I think this is the fault in the DNA of us Indians,” he said. He also appealed to the Himachal Pradesh government to take stronger action against littering. “I would request the Himachal government to take some tough steps,” Raghavan said. He then turned the camera towards the surroundings and added, “It is such a beautiful place. And look what we have done, what filth we have created.”The video showed the garbage collected by Raghavan and the others during their walk. Raghavan also shared a short caption with the video, writing, “We indians are a disgrace. Thank you”. He tagged the official Himachal Tourism and Himachal Police Instagram accounts in the post.What social media users saidThe video prompted reactions from viewers, with several users discussing both littering by tourists and the role of citizens in keeping public places clean. One user wrote, “One of the most stunning countries, destroyed by ‘chalta hai’ mentality.” Another user pointed out that the presence of dustbins does not necessarily stop people from throwing waste on the ground. “The saddest part is they infact do have dustbins at regular intervals on each hiking trail I went on. But people still litter,” the user wrote. Another commenter questioned whether the problem should be placed only on the government, arguing that citizens also have a responsibility to follow rules. “Easy to blame the government, but we citizens aren’t exactly innocent either. articles.title: Bid to run new trains between London and Blackpool rejected
articles.summary: Plans for more trains would “likely increase delays and cancelled trains", the rail regulator says.
articles.body:
Plans for new train services between London and Wrexham, Rochdale and Blackpool have been rejected by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR).

The proposal to add more trains on the West Coast Main Line would "likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers", the regulator said.

It rejected Wrexham, Shropshire and Midlands Railway's application for four daily Wrexham to London Euston return services, as well as Lumo's proposal for up to four return services between Rochdale and Euston on weekdays and Saturdays, and three on Sundays.

Avanti West Coast's plans for additional services between Blackpool and Euston were also denied by the ORR.

The regulator said: "Gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers.

"ORR concluded that adding more services into these windows in the timetable for recovery would reduce that resilience, increasing the risk of disruption spreading to other services and affecting more passengers."

Stephanie Tobyn, from the ORR, said: "New services, destinations and greater choice can bring real benefits for passengers and communities.

"But the West Coast Main Line is already under significant pressure, with performance reflecting limited resilience on a heavily used part of the rail network.

"Our detailed analysis has shown that adding more trains to the current timetable would reduce the ability to recover when disruption occurs, increasing the risk of delays spreading and making reliability of the network worse for all passengers."

The ORR said its assessment and decision came after similar applications were rejected in 2025.

articles.title: Italy overhauls electoral system after fiercely contested debate
articles.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says the move will deliver more stable government, but opposition parties say her aim is to stay in power.
articles.body:
Italy's parliament has approved fiercely contested changes to the country's electoral system championed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni ahead of elections due next year.

Lawmakers voted 227 to 164 in favour of moving to a fully proportional system, which Meloni has argued will boost the chance of clear winners and more stable government.

Opposition parties say her right-wing coalition has designed the proposals to improve its chance of retaining power and, in a heated debate on Thursday, accused it of flouting democracy.

Meloni had warned she could resign and trigger an early election if the plans were rejected, with the secret ballot seen as a test of her authority.

Meloni's coalition has overseen a rare period of political stability for Italy since her election in 2022, and last month her government became the country's longest-running since World War Two.

The voting reform will see the country move away from its current hybrid voting system, in which about a third of members are chosen through a first-past-the-post vote and the rest through proportional representation.

Parties proposing to form a coalition will be required to put forward their joint candidate for prime minister, and their political programme, before any general election.

A party or coalition which emerges with the largest share of the votes - provided this exceeds 42% - will be awarded 105 additional seats in parliament (70 in the lower house and 35 in the senate), which could turn a narrow victory into a more comfortable majority.

In a debate ahead of the vote, centre-left members accused the government of forcing through the new voting rules.

"Go ahead and change the electoral law, we will win in any case under any voting system," said Democratic Party (PD) leader Elly Schlein.

The proposals have also exposed tensions within the ranks of Meloni's coalition, too, with the Brothers of Italy (FdI) party and its allies, the far-right League and centre-right Forza Italia.

Analysts had predicted that Thursday's final vote was unlikely to fail - particularly given the number of lawmakers who would risk losing their eligibility for a parliamentary pension if their term was ended early as a result of the threatened snap election.

"To those who hoped to see the centre-right divided," Meloni wrote on social media after the vote, "today we respond with facts: we are united, cohesive, and determined to carry forward the commitments made to citizens."

She added: "We are introducing rules designed to promote the stability and parliamentary coherence of any government, regardless of its political colour."

Meloni's term officially comes to an end in October 2027, although she could bring elections forward to the spring.

articles.title: Strawberry farmer calls for supermarkets to invest in UK
articles.summary: Bal Padda, from Worcestershire, is calling on supermarkets to make use of British produce.
articles.body:
The owner of a strawberry farm in Worcestershire says the changing climate is extending their growing season, leaving many strawberries unpicked and unsold.

Bal Padda runs the 150-acre Vicarage Nurseries, in Bretforton, and says his business is slowing their operation down due to a drop in demand.

"We're putting it on hold today. We picked yesterday but have no order today. The demand drops down", he said.

"Supermarkets have started importing now, they assume the UK season is over and done with".

But with longer, hotter summers the strawberry season is starting to last longer.

Last year, picking at the nursery ended on 24 November.

This year, Padda said the farm had at least eight weeks of harvesting left, potentially taking production into December.

"That surplus could be used for a secondary thing".

But as things stand this year, many of the ripe strawberries sitting under the 100 polytunnels on the farm may remain unpicked.

articles.title: A trainee solicitor broke a 14-year-old marathon record held by Dracula; Archie Hunt ran 2:27:41 dressed as Captain Underpants
articles.summary: Most marathon runners simply hope to finish in one piece. Archie Hunt wanted to finish fast while wearing little more than a cape and underpants.
articles.body: Most marathon runners simply hope to finish in one piece. Archie Hunt wanted to finish fast while wearing little more than a cape and underpants. Dressed as Captain Underpants, the beloved children's book hero, he ran the London Marathon in 2 hours, 27 minutes, and 41 seconds, beating a record that had stood since 2012 and was held by a runner dressed as Dracula. Here’s how, what Guinness World Records requires, how Hunt trained while working at a law firm, and why his run also carried a serious and personal message about heart health.How Archie Hunt broke the Guinness World Record for fastest marathon dressed as a book characterRoll on Friday reported that Hunt, a trainee at the law firm Milbank, set a new Guinness World Record for the fastest marathon dressed as a book character when he ran the London Marathon as Captain Underpants. Guinness World Records lists the achievement under the title for the fastest marathon dressed as a book character in the male category, with a time of 2 hours, 27 minutes, and 41 seconds, set in London on 26 April 2026. It was one of 38 Guinness World Records titles achieved by participants at the event. Legal Cheek had reported earlier in April that Hunt was aiming to finish in under 2 hours 30 minutes in full costume.The 2 hour 27 minute 41 second finish beat the 2012 Dracula costume recordThe previous record, set in 2012 by a runner dressed as Dracula, stood at 2 hours, 42 minutes, and 17 seconds. Legal Cheek notes that Hunt shaved about 15 minutes off the previous time. For most runners, even a finish under three hours is a career highlight, so a time under 2 hours 30 minutes in a costume is remarkable. Hunt said he finished in the top 0.1 per cent at one of the sport's World Major marathons, something he still found hard to believe.Why Hunt chose Captain Underpants as his choice of book character for the runHunt told Roll on Friday that his choice of costume came backwards, he found the record first and then worked out the costume. Captain Underpants fit well because he is a popular children's book character, which suited the children's charity Hunt was supporting; he is loved by Hunt's younger brother, and he is funny. The rules require that the costume originate in a book. Characters that began in a cartoon, a film, or a television show, or that count as superheroes, belong to separate categories. Legal Cheek adds that the attempt also demands strict adherence to costume guidelines, official timing data, witness statements, and photographic evidence. Hunt joked that the skimpy outfit helped prevent chafing, though a persistent wedgie after mile 17 balanced that out. He also admitted he barely tested the costume beforehand, apart from a few jumps in the garden.How a trainee solicitor trained about 155 kilometres a week for 16 weeksThe record was no accident. Hunt said he trained for 16 weeks, averaging about 155 kilometres a week, along with strength work. He had run roughly 350 laps of Regent's Park that year, and the preparation was not smooth; he had calf trouble in the final weeks and woke up with a cold the Friday before the race. Legal Cheek says he balanced this with life at a top law firm, including early morning runs of more than 20 kilometres before work. His advice to others is to build up slowly, since his own progress took about two years of steady training, and to favour discipline over motivation. For anyone chasing a Guinness World Record, he suggests picking something that plays to your strengths, reading the rules carefully, and choosing a challenge you will still find funny deep into the race.Running with dilated cardiomyopathy, the heart condition behind his charity fundraisingHunt ran to raise money for Evelina London Children's Charity, which is linked to the hospital where he receives treatment for dilated cardiomyopathy, a condition that affects the heart's ability to pump blood efficiently. He has noted that the condition can add 10 to 15 minutes to a marathon time. Hunt said he is proud to be the fastest recorded marathon runner diagnosed with the condition, and that he wants to raise awareness because his own diagnosis came later than it should have. He hopes his story shows others with serious heart conditions that a diagnosis does not have to define their limits. Hunt told Roll on Friday that he sees the charity's work first-hand because he visits the hospital a couple of times a month, which made the fundraising an easy decision.What comes next for Archie Hunt after the recordHunt has no plans to stop. He said a 110-kilometre ultramarathon in Finland is next, and his long-term goal is to finish a marathon in under 2 hours 20 minutes, even if that takes time and means finding a coach other than himself. He also plans to run the Tromso Midnight Sun marathon in June. The co-managing partners of Milbank's London office congratulated him and said the firm could not be prouder.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chrysler Building to get its crown restored after being sold
articles.summary: The distinctive Manhattan skyscraper will undergo a major renovation and provide a new supply of offices.
articles.body:
The Chrysler Building, one of the most distinctive high-rises in Manhattan's skyline, will undergo a major renovation as part of a multi-million-dollar sale deal.

The skyscraper, opened in New York nearly 100 years ago, will see its Art Deco crown polished and restored during a refurbishment that will also involve the restoration of the building's 77-storey façade.

Developer Tishman Speyer has taken over the lease from the Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art, a private college.

Tishman Speyer and its partners will invest $235m (£178m) in the project, as part of which it will upgrade the 61st floor, which is home to huge eagle gargoyles and will also feature an "upscale" lounge.

The developer is planning to use most of the building, which is close to Grand Central railway station, for office space. It is following what it calls a "prebuild approach" that will allow firms to move into their new premises quickly.

Tishman Speyer explained that the area "has one of the lowest office availability rates in Manhattan", adding: "Construction of new office supply in the neighbourhood has been virtually nonexistent for decades."

The renovation will include internal work, such as upgrades to the building's mechanical, elevator, electrical and air handling systems.

At 1,046ft (319m), the Chrysler Building was once the world's tallest building - before being usurped less than a year later by the nearby Empire State Building.

Financed by Walter Chrysler, the motor magnate, the skyscraper's construction began in 1928 and was completed two years later.

Architect William Van Alen modelled the eagle gargoyles on hood ornaments found on the 1929 Chrysler car.

The Cooper Union college, whose alumni include inventor Thomas Edison, has owned the land on which the Chrysler Building stands since 1902.

The land was bequeathed to it by the children of Peter Cooper, a manufacturer and industrialist who founded the college in 1859.

As part of the deal, Tishman Speyer will make ground lease payments to the Cooper Union which the college wants to use to finance "a bold plan to restore full-tuition scholarships for all undergraduates".

Cooper Union's president Steven McLaughlin, said: "The significance of this agreement is ultimately about what it makes possible for generations of Cooper Union students."

articles.title: ‘Not day of politics’: Back as Punjab Cong chief, Pargat first visits Golden Temple, drops in at Giani Tea Stall
articles.summary: Pargat Singh begins Punjab Congress chief role with visits to Amritsar’s Golden Temple, Durgiana Mandir, Balmiki Tirath Sthal and St Paul Church.
articles.body: Amritsar: Newly appointed Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) president Pargat Singh began his first visit to the state after taking charge on Thursday by paying obeisance at prominent religious shrines of Amritsar. He was accompanied by Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot and several senior party functionaries.All Punjab MPs of the Congress were, however, absent as they are part of the party’s protest in Delhi to seek the removal of the chief election commissioner.Pargat, who succeeded Amrinder Singh Raja Warring as Punjab Congress chief on Oct 3, arrived at Amritsar's Sri Guru Ramdas Ji International Airport from Delhi around 9am, where party functionaries and workers welcomed him with drum beats. He then headed straight to the Golden Temple to pay obeisance.Pilot was on the wheel of the car during the visit.Speaking at the Golden Temple, Pargat said he had come to offer thanksgiving and made it clear the day was not meant for political activity. “Today is not a day for politics. I will certainly do politics, but after a day or two,” he said.He later visited the Sri Durgiana Temple, St Paul Church and Bhagwan Valmiki Tirath Sthan in Amritsar. The visits were part of his programme to seek blessings for communal harmony, brotherhood and solidarity before taking charge as Punjab Congress president on Oct 11.He had earlier appealed to party workers and supporters to avoid large gatherings at religious places, so that devotees were not inconvenienced. He also urged them to maintain simplicity and humility during the visits.Sources in the Congress informed that Pargat was likely to hold a meeting with the Punjab Congress leadership in Mohali as part of his initial engagements after taking charge. He is also scheduled to visit the Mata Chintpurni shrine in Himachal Pradesh the following day.Before returning to Punjab, Pargat had met Warring in Delhi. After the meeting, he said the Congress was united in Punjab and differences of opinion were part of democracy.He said the party would unitedly contest the 2027 Punjab assembly elections , signalling that maintaining unity within the state unit would be among his priorities as he begins his tenure as PPCC chief. articles.title: Who is 'cybercrime specialist' Daniel Robson? Canadian publications pulled down his articles after two years because he is possibly AI
articles.summary: Two years after Daniel Robson emerged in the Canadian media scene as an expert in extremism, terrorism, and cybercrime, several Canadian outlets said
articles.body: Two years after Daniel Robson emerged in the Canadian media scene as an expert in extremism, terrorism, and cybercrime, several Canadian outlets said Robson might not be a real person and probably an AI persona. Robson published several articles under his name and photo and even contributed a chapter to a book. But the suspicion was flagged by an editor at Turkiye Today who wanted to do a video call with Robson. Robson refused, prompting the Turkiye Today editor to contact the Canadian editors who published Daniel's articles. Eventually, nobody could establish Daniel's identity.Here's what Canadian media saidAs reported by CBC, Policy Options said last week that it removed an article published last year under Robson's name after it was "unable to independently establish that the person who wrote for us is who he represents himself to be or that the biographical information he provided is accurate."The Ottawa Citizen said it took down Robson's articles after an investigation uncovered that he does not exist.Ottawa Citizen editor-in-chief Nicole Feriancek also said in a written statement on Tuesday that Robson had described himself as a "'Canadian journalist' specializing in extremism, terrorism and crime." But he said Robson's mugshot photo appeared to be AI-generated, and so are his writings.Feriancek said attempts to call or meet Robson were declined. "When we were up front with our concerns, and said we wanted to verify his identity — in person — he declared he was incensed by our line of questions, and he ended all communication."How did the investigation begin?On September 2, Turkiye Today received a 600-word email from Robson which said: “I am writing to submit for your consideration an investigative feature entitled ‘From Canada Through Türkiye: Canadian Runs Criminal Network Linking Drug Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling." The Turkiye Today expose said that the editor who read the email found something fishy and immediately wanted to have a one-on-one video call with him. Managing editor Ilker Sezer said he instantly liked the story as it involved a Moroccan drug lord laundering money through a Turkish middleman and wanted more information.“I have been dealing for several days with a dental problem that recently worsened and developed into significant trismus, with painful restriction of jaw movement. I underwent a minor oral surgical procedure yesterday to address the underlying problem, but the stiffness and discomfort remain quite pronounced, particularly with repeated jaw movement and sustained speaking," Robson repliedThis prompted the digging up and nobody could find out anything real about the person.Then who is Daniel Robson?Sezer said he can't say for sure who is behind the AI journalist but it may have a link to Morocco. The Globe and Mail reported on Wednesday that a digital research tool showed that Robson's email address was used to register a Moroccan Microsoft account in March.
